description:
Programme or Project Overview

UMCG advertises a doctoral (promovendus) position on methodology for passende huisartszorg - appropriate care in general practice - funded through the ZonMw PZL-AWH programme. The project develops and tests methods to measure and improve the appropriateness of care in Dutch general practice: balancing overuse and underuse, embedding shared decision-making, and evaluating how guideline recommendations translate into everyday primary care. The position is a salaried four-year PhD employment with a starting salary of EUR 3,217 per month.

The candidate works within UMCG's primary-care research environment, which combines registry research, practice-based fieldwork and methodological innovation, and collaborates with the national ZonMw programme community. Because the research involves Dutch general practices and patient data, command of Dutch is required. The doctoral training runs through the UMCG Graduate School of Medical Sciences with a supervisory team spanning primary care, epidemiology and implementation science.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in health sciences, epidemiology, medicine or a related discipline, with interest in care-appropriateness research and methodological rigour. Experience with registry data, measurement development or qualitative methods is an advantage. Applications are submitted through the werkenbijumcg.nl portal, and the closing date is 4 November 2026.

Highlights

  • ZonMw-funded PhD on appropriate care methodology in general practice
  • Overuse, underuse and shared decision-making research
  • Registry research plus practice-based fieldwork
  • Salaried four-year position (EUR 3,217 - 4,077 per month)
  • UMCG Graduate School of Medical Sciences training
  • Dutch proficiency required; closing date 4 November 2026

About University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG)

UMCG is one of the largest university medical centres in the Netherlands and the academic hospital of the University of Groningen. It combines patient care with biomedical research and graduate education, organised around research institutes covering neuroscience, oncology, ageing, regenerative medicine and population health. The centre employs PhD candidates and postdocs on salaried contracts under the Dutch collective agreement for university medical centres (CAO-UMC). Research and clinical vacancies, including physician-researcher tracks and technical R&D roles, are published on its recruitment portal werkenbijumcg.nl.
